summary: .QL is an object-oriented query language developed by Semmle for querying source code as a relational database. It later became the basis of GitHub's CodeQL.
notableFor: Basis of GitHub's CodeQL

summary: The Formula language is a scripting language used in Lotus Notes. Many of its language elements begin with the @ character, which is why it is also called @Formula.
A+ is an array programming language derived from APL. It was first released in 1988.
The A-0 System was an early compiler-related tool written by Grace Murray Hopper in 1951 and 1952 for the UNIVAC I. It functioned more as a loader or linker than as a modern compiler.
notableFor: Early compiler-related tool by Grace Murray Hopper

summary: A# (listed here as A.NET) is a port of the Ada programming language to Microsoft's .NET platform. It was distributed by the Department of Computer Science at the United States Air Force Academy under the GNU General Public License.
ABAP is a domain-specific high-level programming language created by SAP SE. It is used, alongside Java, to program the SAP NetWeaver Application Server.
notableFor: SAP's language for the NetWeaver Application Server

summary: ABC is a structured, imperative teaching language developed at CWI in Amsterdam in the 1980s as an alternative to BASIC and Pascal for beginners. Its design influenced the Python language.
notableFor: Influenced the design of Python

summary: Action! is a structured, ALGOL-like programming language for the Atari 8-bit computers. It was released in 1983 by Optimized Systems Software.
notableFor: Language for Atari 8-bit computers

summary: ActionScript is an object-oriented programming language originally developed by Macromedia. It is influenced by HyperTalk and is now an implementation of ECMAScript.
notableFor: Originally used for Flash content

summary: Actor is a programming language invented by Charles Duff of The Whitewater Group in 1988. It was an offshoot of object-oriented extensions he had developed for the Forth language.
notableFor: Object-oriented extensions to Forth

summary: AdvPL is a proprietary programming language based on xBase. It was released in 1999 and is used to develop applications for the Protheus ERP system from TOTVS.
notableFor: Used for TOTVS Protheus ERP

summary: Agda is a dependently typed functional programming language. The current version, Agda 2, is a full rewrite of the original system developed at Chalmers in 1999.
notableFor: Dependently typed functional language and proof assistant

summary: Keysight VEE, originally Agilent VEE and earlier HP VEE, is a graphical dataflow programming environment. It is used for automated test, measurement, data analysis and reporting.
notableFor: Graphical dataflow environment for test and measurement

summary: AIMMS is a commercial modelling language and environment for mathematical optimization and decision support. It was first released in 1993.

Alef is a discontinued concurrent programming language designed by Phil Winterbottom at Bell Labs as part of the Plan 9 operating system. It implemented the channel-based concurrency of Newsqueak in a compiled, C-like language.
notableFor: Designed for the Plan 9 operating system

summary: Algebraic Logic Functional (ALF) is a programming language that combines functional and logic programming. Its foundation is Horn clause logic with equality.
ALGOL 58, originally named IAL, is an early member of the ALGOL family of programming languages. It was an early compromise design that was soon superseded by ALGOL 60.
ALGOL 60 is an imperative, block-structured programming language defined in 1960 by an international committee. Its report introduced Backus-Naur form notation.
notableFor: Introduced block structure and Backus-Naur form in its report

summary: ALGOL 68 is an imperative member of the ALGOL family, conceived as a successor to ALGOL 60. It had a much wider scope of application and more rigorously defined syntax and semantics.

Alice ML is a general-purpose, multi-paradigm functional programming language designed at Saarland University in Germany. It is a dialect of Standard ML augmented with lazy evaluation, concurrency and constraint programming.
notableFor: Standard ML dialect with lazy evaluation and concurrency

summary: Alma-0 is a multi-paradigm programming language that augments the imperative Modula-2 language with logic programming features and backtracking. It combines constraint programming with imperative and declarative styles.
AmbientTalk is an experimental object-oriented distributed programming language developed at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel in Belgium. It is aimed at programs deployed in mobile ad hoc networks.
notableFor: Designed for mobile ad hoc networks

summary: Amiga E is a programming language created by Wouter van Oortmerssen for the Amiga computer. Work began in 1991, and the first release came in 1993.
notableFor: Created for the Amiga computer

summary: AMPL is an algebraic modeling language for describing and solving large-scale mathematical optimization problems. It was developed by Robert Fourer, David Gay and Brian Kernighan at Bell Laboratories.
notableFor: Algebraic modeling language for optimization

summary: Analitik is a programming language developed in 1968 at the Institute of Cybernetics of the Academy of Sciences of the Ukrainian SSR. It is a development of the ALMIR-65 language and keeps compatibility with it.
AngelScript is an embeddable scripting language for C++ applications, created by Andreas Jonsson. It was first released in 2003.
notableFor: Embeddable scripting language for C++ applications

summary: Pig Latin is the language of Apache Pig, a high-level platform for creating programs that run on Apache Hadoop. It abstracts Java MapReduce programming into a notation similar to SQL.
notableFor: Language of Apache Pig on Hadoop

summary: Apex is a proprietary, Java-like programming language for building applications on the Salesforce platform. It is used to write server-side logic in the Salesforce environment.
notableFor: Salesforce platform language

summary: APL is a programming language developed in the 1960s by Kenneth E. Iverson, centred on multidimensional arrays. It uses a large set of special symbols to express functions and operators concisely.
notableFor: Concise notation based on special symbols and arrays

summary: App Inventor's visual block language lets users build Android apps by joining graphical blocks instead of writing text code. It originated as a 2010 project and is now maintained by MIT.
notableFor: Block-based language for building Android apps

summary: AppleScript is a scripting language created by Apple that facilitates automated control of Mac applications. It was first introduced in System 7.
notableFor: Automates Mac applications

summary: APT is a high-level programming language most commonly used to generate instructions for numerically controlled machine tools. It was developed at MIT, with Douglas T. Ross leading the early effort from 1956.
notableFor: Numerical control of machine tools

summary: Arc is a dialect of Lisp developed by Paul Graham and Robert Morris. It is free and open-source software released under the Artistic License 2.0.
notableFor: Lisp dialect by Paul Graham and Robert Morris

summary: ARexx is a Rexx interpreter for the Amiga, written in 1987 by William S. Hawes. It adds Amiga-specific features that let scripts send commands to applications through their ARexx ports.
notableFor: Rexx interpreter for the Amiga
